## Quality gates

The gates are in CONTRIBUTING.md, "Quality gates", each with its reason.

- [ ] **The picture is never lowered for speed.** No smaller console profile, no lowered render resolution.
- [ ] **A bug fix starts from a failing fixture.** It failed before the change, passes after, and is committed with
      it (a port or a feature behind an off switch may be tested after).
- [ ] **Off means off.** With its switch off the default path is unchanged byte for byte; I said how I checked.
- [ ] **A loop cap is a diagnostic.** No loop limit was raised to make a hang or a slow frame go away.
- [ ] **Tests are not weakened.** No test was removed or weakened; anything that looked wrong is said on the issue.
- [ ] **The commands pass.** Both clippy runs, both test runs, `cargo xtask policy`; the harness tests and `bash -n`
      for a harness change.
- [ ] **GPU tests run on the software adapter while you work.** Then the full commands once on my card.
- [ ] **A fixture that can stall a queue refuses a card.**
- [ ] **A measured claim names its tool.** Figures before and after, and the established tool (docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md).
- [ ] **Tested on a named card, and the others still pass.** The `Tested on:` line above, and how the other vendors
      are covered.
- [ ] **A risky change gets one review from another model family.** Named here, for shader translation, the memory
      model or anything on by default that changes the picture.
- [ ] **Lock, race and memory-ordering work starts from a design note.** Linked here, with its review.
- [ ] **Nothing from the title is committed.** No captures, assets, executable bytes, shader dumps, decompiled or
      disassembled code, or bulk extracted table; a shader is named beside its 16-hex id where that helps.

## Review

- [ ] Reviewed by someone other than the author.
